data.title: NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director | NVIDIA Newsroom
data.summary: NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United [...] “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” [...] “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period.

data.title: Nvidia Still Faces Issues That Cost $2 Trillion in Market Value
data.summary: Huang's reinstatement as CEO after being ousted for a series of alleged affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, solved Nvidia's leadership problem. But it didn't address any of the other issues that were already pressuring the stock, the biggest being whether the company's customers will keep spending heavily on artificial intelligence amid rising skepticism about the returns on those investments. Competition is coming from chipmakers such as Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Broadcom Inc., as well as Nvidia's customers like Alphabet Inc.'s Google.

data.summary: How important is Huang and Nvidia to the AI industry and the US economy?published at 14:22 GMT Michael Race Business and economics reporter There was an air of uncertainty over the future of Nvidia following Huang's initial departure just 11 days ago. Huang played a major role in the company, leading its shift towards AI, and maintained a firm grip, with up to 200 people directly reporting to him. [...] Not only does it sell microchips to its customers, which include the likes of Meta, SpaceX and OpenAI, it has also provided funds for them and other firms in the supply chain by either handing out loans or investing in them directly. There were concerns how that model would work in a world without Huang, which was perhaps why tech bosses including Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, the CEO of Fortnite maker Epic Games, called for Huang's reinstatement. [...] He also was a key player in drumming up enthusiasm and investment for the wider AI industry and so his departure, according to some, posed a risk to future investment. That is because Nvidia, on its journey to the top of the microchip making industry, has created a spider's web of deals through what is known as "circular financing".
